create.name: Choe Khor Sum Ling
create.bio:
Choe Khor Sum Ling, usually shortened to CKSL, is a Tibetan Mahayana Buddhist centre in Bengaluru, in the Domlur area of the city. Local students started it after the Dalai Lama asked Lama Zopa Rinpoche to support a centre there, and it is affiliated with the FPMT, so it uses that network's study programmes, drawn from the teaching of its two founding lamas. The Dalai Lama gave the centre its name, a reference to the Buddha's three successive rounds of teaching.

Its resident teachers are Western and Indian monastics who are studying, or have completed, the geshe programme at Sera Jey Monastery in Karnataka, among them Geshe Tenzin Namdak and Venerables Tenzin Legtsok, Tenzin Namjong, Gyalten Rabten and Gyalten Lekden. Classes run as sequential courses on lamrim, mind training, the Heart and Diamond Sutras, Shantideva and mindfulness, held at the small temple and live on Zoom, and the centre keeps a lending library of Dharma books. Its YouTube channel, active since 2010, posts full recordings of these classes and of visiting teachers, usually as long multi-part series.

flags: The website is a single page last updated around 2020–21: its course and event listings are all past, so no offerings or free resources could be taken from it. The channel is active (uploads to 7 Nov 2026), so the listing rests on its 12 videos. Owner may want to hold it until the site is current.
Email is the centre's general inbox (info@cksl.in), published on the home page.

Teachers file is empty: none of the teachers the site names (Geshe Tenzin Namdak, Ven. Tenzin Legtsok, Ven. Tenzin Namjong, Ven. Gyalten Rabten, Ven. Gyalten Lekden, Ven. Thubten Kalden, Geshe Ngawang Norbu) is on Spiritpedia. Possible future listings: Geshe Tenzin Namdak, Venerable Tenzin Legtsok.
Venerable Thubten Chodron gives one of the chosen talks; she is not on Spiritpedia.
Photo is the channel avatar, the centre's own emblem with its name.
